rationale: The numerator omits depreciation, so "cash available" is systematically understated for capital-intensive firms and the signal collapses to roughly minus (accruals + investment intensity) scaled by liabilities — i.e. a mechanical blend of the published Sloan accruals and capex/asset-growth anomalies — while also being a near-rescale of the archived Post-Investment Obligation Surplus.

This is the archived "Cash Resources Versus Committed Uses" with oancf swapped for an inferior (dp-omitting) accrual proxy of cash flow, which is an input substitution rather than a new economic claim, and the coverage gain is bought at the cost of a noisier and downward-biased numerator.

target_name: Conjunctive Coverage Of Investment And Claims
rationale: A coherent full-coverage recombination of two archived winners whose one substantive innovation — putting the firm's own capex into the liquidity denominator so the required cash buffer scales with committed investment — is defensible, though the design is close enough to Smooth Funding Capacity Product that a null result would be uninformative.

target_name: Earnings Coverage Where Investment Is Largest
rationale: The double-MIN difference genuinely centers to zero at median coverage and at low investment, so it isolates the profitability-by-investment interaction rather than either main effect, the expected positive sign matches the algebra, and the conditioning axis (capex intensity) differs economically from the archived leverage-conditioned version.

An uncentered product of two positively-signed ranks loads heavily on its main effects — capx/ppent is the published investment anomaly and short-term-debt reliance/debt-maturity structure has documented return effects contrary to the "no unconditional effect" claim — and this is the fourth conditioner bolted onto the same capx/ppent leg that has repeatedly delivered weak alphas in this archive.

target_name: Coverage Gap Amplified By Short Maturity Reliance
rationale: Sign and construction are internally consistent (low coverage × high short-maturity share = high score = negative expected return) and the maturity-share conditioner is a genuinely untested axis, but the score inherits the dp-omission flaw of Signal 1's numerator, the product remains main-effect contaminated, and zero-debt firms drop out of the denominator, selectively removing the safest names.
